title: On‑Prem Customer Handoff + Outstanding Blockers (Apr 2026)
content:
Summary and purpose:
This doc captures the on‑prem deployment handoff for Customer X42, the weekly standup notes from the install window (2026‑04‑09 to 2026‑04‑11), and an explicit list of unresolved technical blockers that are currently preventing final signoff. Aim is to have clear owners and next actions so Solutions Eng and SRE can coordinate with the customer and avoid a prolonged support loop.

Attendees (internal):
- Maya Thompson (Solutions Eng)
- Diego Alvarez (SRE)
- Priya Raman (Networking, infra)
- Liam Chen (Servicing/runtime)
- Aisha Beg (Security/compliance)

Customer contacts:
- Tom H. (Infra lead, X42)
- Noor S. (Security)
- Deployment window: engineers onsite remote support 2026‑04‑14 -> 2026‑04‑16 (tentative)

Key install components covered:
- Private agent (v0.9.3) container images pulled from customer registry
- On‑prem orchestrator config (k8s 1.25 static manifests)
- VPC peering / cross‑site routing (BGP session with customer edge)
- KMS integration (customer HSM using PKCS#11 shim)
- NTP/time sync and signed cert issuance via ACME internal CA

Standup notes (high level) 2026‑04‑09:
- Diego: node provisioning mostly green; 3 of 12 worker nodes failed driver (NVIDIA 535) detection during kubelet start on R640 hosts. Happening when host kernel is 5.15.x. Ticket RINF‑2410 created.
- Priya: customer ACLs blocking our healthcheck probes (TCP 8081/8082) from control plane; they set a deny rule for ephemeral ports. Customer to open 8081/8082 and allow source CIDR 10.32.0.0/21.
- Maya: private agent image access — customer registry had an MFA policy; eng requested a short‑lived access token and we verified pull works when using service principal. Action: customer to create pull role with expiry >= 7 days.
- Liam: kv cache warmup failing for models with >6B params due to memory accounting mismatch (OOM on init). Workaround: set MODEL_INIT_RAM_LIMIT env var to 36G for now.

Standup notes 2026‑04‑10:
- Security (Aisha): HSM integration succeeded for envelope keys but signing API latency spikes when HSM is under load. Customer will run HSM in HA mode; until then we should add client retry/backoff in private agent (low effort).
- Network: observed MTU mismatch between customer WAN (9000) and private agent default (1500) causing fragmentation on large KV sync payloads. Priya to push mtu=9000 to host network config and confirm.
- Diego: 2 nodes failing kubelet due to systemd cgroup setting; host boots with cgroup v1 compatibility flag disabled. Need host change (grub kernel arg) or run kubelet with --cgroup-driver=systemd fallback.

Standup notes 2026‑04‑11 (handoff meeting):
- Customer asked for a one‑page runbook for day‑2 ops: scaling workers, force cache flush, rollback image. Draft created and attached as linked artifact (GH gist in thread).
- Discussed SLA expectations: until Dedicated/Private contract signed, X42 will be on engineering support (no SLA). Customer accepted but asked for 24h follow during first 30 days.
- Decided on action owners and priorities (see below).

Outstanding technical blockers (explicit list):
1) Node driver detection failure on R640 hosts (RINF‑2410) 
   - Symptom: kubelet fails to register GPU devices; container runtime rejects gpu plugin socket.
   - Temporary workaround: install nvidia‑driver 535.86.05-1 on affected nodes; restart kubelet.
   - Owner: Diego Alvarez.
   - ETA: 2026‑04‑14 (during remote maintenance window).

2) Customer firewall dropping healthcheck probes (RINF‑2345)
   - Symptom: control plane reports unhealthy for private agent, autoscaling disabled.
   - Ask: open TCP 8081/8082 from control plane CIDR (35.200.128.0/20) and allow ephemeral response ports.
   - Owner: Tom H. (customer) / Priya (supporting config).
   - Blocking signoff.

3) MTU mismatch and large payload fragmentation
   - Symptom: KV sync stalls and retries lead to timeouts for model loads > 6B.
   - Plan: update host MTU to 9000 OR enable jumbo frame negotiation on virtual switch; also add path MTU discovery logs.
   - Owner: Priya Raman / X42 network team.

4) HSM performance causing intermittent signing latency spikes
   - Symptom: spikes up to 400ms for envelope signing causing request latency tail.
   - Mitigation: client backoff and local signing cache (short TTL 2s) implemented in branch private-agent#412.
   - Owner: Aisha Beg (security), Liam Chen (implement local cache).

5) MODEL_INIT_RAM_LIMIT mismatch causing OOM on large models
   - Short term: set env var to 36G on large model jobs.
   - Long term: investigate memory accounting on allocator path in runtime (L2 profiling).
   - Owner: Liam Chen.

Decisions and reasons:
- We will not delay the whole installation for node driver mismatch; proceed with partial capacity (9/12 nodes) & allow customer to sign off on degraded capacity for initial traffic. Rationale: unblock QA and app integration early.
- KMS changes must be audited; Aisha to add required CloudTrail/HSM logs to handoff checklist.

Immediate next steps (owners and times):
- Priya: confirm opening 8081/8082 with Tom by 2026‑04‑12 EOD (Slack thread).
- Diego: prepare driver install plan and rollback steps, test on 1 node, target 2026‑04‑14 maintenance window.
- Liam: merge local signing cache patch to private-agent main (PR #412) and publish canary image, ETA 2026‑04‑13.
- Aisha: update runbook with HSM operational notes (rotation, failover) by 2026‑04‑12.
- Maya: schedule next customer sync 2026‑04‑13 to validate action completion and agree on signoff checklist.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Does X42 have a central observability forwarder for our tracer spans? (they currently have Splunk, need OTLP collector config).
- Confirm backup plan for key material if on‑prem HSM needs emergency replacement—can we failover to cloud KMS temporarily? (compliance check pending).

Notes to self / internal reminders:
- Capture exact kernel version on failed nodes and attach to RINF‑2410.
- Add a short blurb in the private deployments playbook about MTU issues — we keep hitting this in >1 customer.
- Follow up with infra release‑engineering about packaging a driver install helper script for R640 fleet.

Attachments / artifacts referenced in meeting:
- Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-2345 (firewall rules)
- Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-2410 (GPU driver detection)
- PR: GitHub: redwood-inference/private-agent#412 (local signing cache)
- Slack thread: #private-deploys (thread ts: 1712870400.000200)

Handoff checklist (for customer signoff):
- [ ] All healthcheck ports opened and verified from control plane
- [ ] Minimum 9/12 worker nodes in Ready state with GPU visible
- [ ] KMS/HSM keys provisioned and test encrypt/decrypt passed
- [ ] NTP drift < 50ms across cluster
- [ ] Runbook acknowledged by customer (Tom H.)

If any of the above items remain open on 2026‑04‑16 we will escalate to Eng PM and schedule an on‑call war‑room.

End notes: this doc should be updated after the 2026‑04‑13 follow‑up sync. Put final signoff (customer acceptance) as a short appendix with timestamp and name when done.

Maya Thompson
Solutions Engineering — Private Deployments
